sentences.text: Zuniceratops possessed a long, low snout similar to chasmosaurines, a thin wide frill resembling a shield, and a partial proximal parietal bone with an inverted T-shape like Protoceratops.
This dinosaur was discovered in 1996 by an eight-year-old boy named Christopher James Wolfe.
While the first discovered specimen of Zuniceratops had unusual single-rooted teeth, larger fossils show double-rooted teeth, indicating that teeth became double-rooted with age.
Zuniceratops lived during the Turonian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now New Mexico, United States, approximately 94 million years ago.
The time range for Zuniceratops is the Turonian stage, from 93.9 to 89.8 million years ago.
